title: Submission, Quote, and Bind, Automated by AI Agents
summary: FurtherAI's AI agents carry submissions from broker email to quote and bind, with underwriters approving risk and setting price. See how it works.
body_markdown:
FurtherAI now runs the full submission-quote-bind workflow with AI agents. From the moment a broker's email lands, FurtherAI clears the submission, collects what's missing, triages it, rates it, and carries it through to a quote and a bound policy. Underwriters step in wherever judgment is needed: they approve the risk and set the price.


Teams running FurtherAI in production are seeing:


- **2x more underwriting capacity**
- **80% reduction in turnaround time**
- [30x faster submission intake](https://www.furtherai.com/customers/submissions-processing-ai)


‍ **Why submission-quote-bind needs a new approach**


Managing general agents (MGAs) and carriers live on submission, quote, and bind. Consequently, how fast you move through it decides how much business you win. Yet most of the hours go to busywork: checking for duplicate submissions, chasing brokers for loss runs, reading ACORD forms, keying data into rating worksheets, and building quote documents. We built FurtherAI to hand that work to AI agents, so underwriters can focus on the decisions only they can make.


## **How FurtherAI runs submission-quote-bind**


Here's the workflow on a small commercial account from our demo: a hardware store applying for a businessowners package.


### 1. Intake and triage, in under five minutes


A broker email arrives with an ACORD 125, an ACORD 140, and a supplemental application. FurtherAI then:


1. **Clears the submission** against past submissions.
2. **Collects missing documents** , such as loss runs from the agency.
3. **Reads every document** in the file.
4. **Checks underwriting guidelines** and flags anything for review.
5. **Scores and prioritizes the submission** , so the best-fit risks rise to the top of the queue.


For more on this stage, see our guides to[submission clearance](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/what-is-submission-clearance) and[Inbox Agent](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/introducing-inbox-agent-the-first-step-of-underwriting-handled-before-anyone-opens-the-email) .


### 2. Underwriters approve the risk


After triage, FurtherAI asks for approval where underwriter judgment is needed. The underwriter records a decision, such as sending the account to rating, notes the referral basis, and adds context for the quote. The decision is logged against their name. The risk call stays with the underwriter, and FurtherAI makes sure they have everything in front of them when they make it.


### 3. Rated automatically, priced by your team


FurtherAI runs rating and produces a worksheet with an indicated premium. Your underwriter then sets the final price, applying schedule modifications and selecting optional coverages, and issues the quote in one click.


### 4. A quote in your brand, ready to send


FurtherAI generates the quotation in your own branding, ready to go to the broker, and carries the account through to a bound policy.


## **Every number traces back to its source**


Speed only helps if underwriters trust the output. **Every value FurtherAI extracts links back to the exact place it came from in the source file.** Click the building limit on the account, and you see the line on the ACORD 140 where it was read.


That makes each decision easy to stand behind, whether it's an underwriter checking a figure or an auditor reviewing the file.


## **What this means for your underwriting team**


When agents handle the busywork, underwriting capacity goes up without adding headcount, and brokers get faster answers. At[a U.S. MGA writing more than $1.5 billion in premium](https://www.furtherai.com/customers/submissions-processing-ai) , the average time to clear a submission fell from about 32 minutes to about one, and the team saved more than 2,000 hours of manual work in its first three months.


Submission-quote-bind runs from start to finish, performed by AI and guided by underwriters at every point where their judgment counts.
